text: The study examined mutation-specific breast and ovarian cancer risks among BRCA1 and BRCA2 carriers using mutation type, function, and nucleotide position.
The international sample included 19,581 BRCA1 mutation carriers and 11,900 BRCA2 mutation carriers from 55 centers in 33 countries.
Researchers estimated RHR, the ratio of breast versus ovarian cancer hazard ratios, where values greater than one indicated elevated breast cancer risk.
The study identified BRCA1 breast cancer cluster regions and an ovarian cancer cluster region around exon 11.
With appropriate validation, mutation-location findings may support cancer risk assessment and prevention decision making for BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers.
With inappropriate validation, mutation-location findings may support cancer risk assessment and prevention decision making for BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutation carriers.
Urology has faced major challenges aligning research processes for new interventions with Evidence-Based Medicine, similar to other branches of surgery.
From an inside perspective, the article explains the IDEAL framework and shows how its recommendations may affect evaluation of current controversial urological procedures.
The conventional framework for trials of new treatments is largely drug-based, so evaluating surgical innovations with the same template can create significant problems.
Randomized trials of surgical techniques are difficult, and case series remain an important feature of the scientific literature.
The IDEAL recommendations provide an alternative approach to study designs appropriate for the specific problems of new surgical techniques.
The IDEAL recommendations provide an alternative approach to study designs inappropriate for the specific problems of new surgical techniques.
RFID devices are increasingly important for patient safety in hospitals, especially for identifying patients during magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scanning.
The study tested sixty I-Code SLI RFID tags with aluminum-etched or copper-etched antennas during MRI and CT imaging procedures.
Signal loss, material movement, heating, and data integrity were assessed in 1.5 T and 3 T MR systems and CT scanning.
No memory loss or data alteration occurred after MRI and CT scanning, and heating or device movement showed no relevant influence.
Patients wearing RFID wristbands are safe in 1.5 T and 3 T MR scanners using normal operation mode for RF-field.
Patients wearing RFID wristbands are dangerous in 1.5 T and 3 T MR scanners using normal operation mode for RF-field.
The development of a safe and effective HIV vaccine remains one of the most important and challenging goals in HIV-AIDS research.
A poxvirus vector prime and envelope protein boost strategy showed modest but statistically significant vaccine efficacy.
Recent progress established the concept that a vaccine could prevent HIV infection.
Two recombinant adenovirus serotype-5 vaccine concepts raised concern that such vaccines might increase susceptibility to HIV infection.
The concern extended to other recombinant adenovirus vectors and other vector-based vaccines currently in development.
The development of a safe and ineffective HIV vaccine remains one of the most important and challenging goals in HIV-AIDS research.
Ovarian cancer is highly lethal among gynecological cancers, and epithelial ovarian cancer has an immunosuppressive microenvironment with disappointing immune therapy responses.
Clinically relevant DNMTi and HDACi doses reduced the immune suppressive microenvironment through type I IFN signaling in a mouse EOC model.
Type I IFN signaling was required for effective in vivo antitumorigenic actions of the DNMTi 5-azacytidine.
AZA increased CD45-positive immune cells, active CD8-positive T cells, and natural killer cells while reducing tumor burden and extending survival.
A triple DNMTi/HDACi plus α-PD-1 combination provided the best antitumor effect in the murine ovarian cancer model.
A triple DNMTi/HDACi plus α-PD-1 combination provided the worst antitumor effect in the murine ovarian cancer model.
Capsule endoscopy was evaluated in adults with acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage presenting to emergency departments at two academic medical centers.
Patients ingested a wireless video capsule, followed by nasogastric tube aspiration and later esophagogastroduodenoscopy.
Capsule endoscopy detected upper gastrointestinal blood significantly more often than nasogastric tube aspiration in enrolled patients.
Capsule endoscopy and EGD showed no significant difference in identifying peptic or inflammatory lesions.
In emergency department patients with acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage, capsule endoscopy appeared feasible and safe and may facilitate triage and earlier endoscopy.
In emergency department patients with acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage, capsule endoscopy appeared feasible and dangerous and may facilitate triage and earlier endoscopy.
Hypoplastic left heart syndrome remains a lethal congenital cardiac defect, and intracoronary autologous cardiosphere-derived cells may improve ventricular function.
The TICAP trial tested whether intracoronary delivery of CDCs was feasible and safe in patients with hypoplastic left heart syndrome.
Fourteen patients were assigned to receive autologous CDC infusion after staged procedures, followed by seven controls receiving standard palliation alone.
CDC-treated patients showed improved right ventricular ejection fraction, better somatic growth, reduced heart failure status, and lower coil occlusion incidence.
Intracoronary infusion of autologous CDCs seemed feasible and safe in children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome after staged surgery in TICAP.
Intracoronary infusion of autologous CDCs seemed feasible and dangerous in children with hypoplastic left heart syndrome after staged surgery in TICAP.
Differentiation therapy targets specific hematologic malignancies, including all-trans retinoic acid treatment for acute promyelocytic leukemia.
The authors predicted that compounds inducing terminal megakaryocyte differentiation would be effective therapies for acute megakaryocytic leukemia.
Such agents might reduce abnormal hematopoietic cell burden in primary myelofibrosis and alter megakaryocyte differentiation in myelodysplastic syndromes.
High-throughput screening identified molecules promoting terminal megakaryocyte differentiation, including polyploidization, where cells accumulate DNA to 32N or greater.
Clinical studies of polyploidy inducers, including aurora kinase A inhibitors, were underway for malignancies, with AMKL and PMF trials in development.
The authors predicted that compounds inducing terminal megakaryocyte differentiation would be ineffective therapies for acute megakaryocytic leukemia.
The workshop discussed humoral immune responses to HIV and vaccine designs that induce viral neutralizing or otherwise protective antibody responses.
Most effective viral vaccines work partly by generating antibodies that inactivate or neutralize invading viruses.
An effective HIV-1 vaccine should elicit potent antiviral neutralizing antibodies, but HIV-1 evades antibody responses and chronically replicates in hosts.
Current HIV vaccine immunogens elicit antibodies that neutralize a minority of circulating HIV-1 isolates.
The main neutralizing antibody targets are gp120 and gp41 envelope glycoproteins, which mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion.
Current HIV vaccine immunogens elicit antibodies that neutralize a majority of circulating HIV-1 isolates.
The study identified the Polymeal as an alternative to the Polypill for reducing cardiovascular disease using literature-based dietary ingredients.
The evidence-based recipe included wine, fish, dark chocolate, fruits, vegetables, garlic, and almonds as ingredients for the Polymeal.
Life tables from Framingham datasets modeled Polymeal benefits in the general population from age 50 using multiplicative correlations.
Combining Polymeal ingredients was estimated to reduce cardiovascular disease events by 76% and increase life expectancy in men and women.
The Polymeal was described as an effective, non-pharmacological, safe, cheap, and tasty alternative for reducing cardiovascular morbidity.
The Polymeal was described as an effective, non-pharmacological, dangerous, cheap, and tasty alternative for reducing cardiovascular morbidity.
The study examined food tolerances and intolerances affecting Crohn's disease symptoms in a New Zealand Caucasian population.
An extensive dietary questionnaire recorded self-reported tolerances and intolerances for 257 food items across 15 food groups.
Frequently beneficial foods included white fish, salmon, tuna, gluten-free products, oatmeal, bananas, boiled potatoes, pumpkin, soya milk, and yoghurt.
Typically detrimental foods included grapefruit, chilli sauce, corn products, peanuts, cream, salami, curried foods, cola drinks, high energy drinks, beer, and red wine.
The wide range of detrimental food items suggested that dietary maintenance of remission was likely to be difficult for Crohn's disease patients.
Typically detrimental foods included grapefruit, chilli sauce, corn products, peanuts, cream, salami, curried foods, cola drinks, low energy drinks, beer, and red wine.
The POBASCAM randomized trial assessed whether HPV DNA testing during the first cervical screen reduced later detection of CIN grade 3 or worse.
Women aged 29-56 years in the Netherlands received HPV DNA and cytology co-testing or cytology testing alone during cervical screening.
At the second screen, CIN grade 3 or worse and cervical cancer were less common in the intervention group.
Among older women with ASCUS, HPV testing remained sensitive for detecting CIN 3 and cancer, with fewer referrals than younger women.
Implementation of HPV DNA testing led to earlier detection of clinically relevant CIN grade 2 or worse and improved cervical cancer protection.
Among older women with ASCUS, HPV testing remained insensitive for detecting CIN 3 and cancer, with fewer referrals than younger women.
The review summarized clinical applications of HPV testing for cervical cancer prevention, including ASCUS triage, post-treatment surveillance, and primary screening.
HPV triage with Hybrid Capture 2 was more sensitive than repeat cytology for women with equivocal Pap smear results.
APTIMA testing was similarly sensitive but more specific than Hybrid Capture 2 for triage of low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.
Primary hrHPV screening detected more CIN2, CIN3, or cancer than cytology, but it was less specific.
Specificity loss from primary HPV-based screening can be compensated by appropriate algorithms involving reflex cytology and HPV16 or HPV18 genotyping.
Specificity loss from primary HPV-based screening can be compensated by inappropriate algorithms involving reflex cytology and HPV16 or HPV18 genotyping.
The study evaluated HPV DNA testing for detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 or cancer in primary cervical screening.
Women in Washington State were screened with thin-layer Pap testing and HPV DNA testing using PCR and signal amplification methods.
Women with high-risk HPV types or ASCUS-or-higher Pap results were referred for colposcopy and biopsy.
HPV DNA testing was more sensitive than thin-layer Pap screening for detecting CIN 3 or higher.
Testing for HPV had higher sensitivity but lower specificity than thin-layer Pap screening in some cervical screening settings.
HPV DNA testing was less sensitive than thin-layer Pap screening for detecting CIN 3 or higher.
The randomized trial studied neurological development in children who received dietary counseling aimed at atherosclerosis prevention since infancy.
Parents received counseling to keep children's diets low in saturated fat and cholesterol during the first five years of life.
At age five, children underwent neurodevelopmental testing, while nutrient intake, serum lipid concentrations, and neurological development were compared between groups.
Intervention children consumed less total fat, saturated fatty acids, and cholesterol than control children at age five.
Repeated child-targeted dietary counseling lessened serum cholesterol increases and was compatible with normal neurological development.
Parents received counseling to keep children's diets high in saturated fat and cholesterol during the first five years of life.
The study screened patients with aortic coarctation using brain MRA to estimate the prevalence of intracranial aneurysms.
Consecutive patients older than 16 years with coarctation underwent brain MRA using a 1.5T scanner and time-of-flight protocol.
Intracranial aneurysms were found in 12 of 117 patients, with a mean aneurysm diameter of 3.9 mm.
Hypertension was more common among patients with intracranial aneurysms than among those without intracranial aneurysms.
Patients with coarctation had a higher prevalence of intracranial aneurysms, occurring earlier than in population studies.
Hypertension was less common among patients with intracranial aneurysms than among those without intracranial aneurysms.
The study examined vitamin D status and biological correlates in postmenopausal women referred for bone mineral density evaluation.
Low vitamin D was associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism and reduced bone mineral density, fracture risk, and fall risk.
Serum measurements included calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, parathyroid hormone, osteocalcin, and betacrosslaps.
Most women had vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency, while only a small proportion had sufficient vitamin D levels.
Vitamin D insufficiency was prevalent and under-treated, possibly leading to secondary hyperparathyroidism in postmenopausal women.
High vitamin D was associated with secondary hyperparathyroidism and reduced bone mineral density, fracture risk, and fall risk.
The meta-analysis assessed gestational diabetes mellitus risk according to prepregnancy maternal body mass index across observational studies from the previous 30 years.
Electronic database searches accepted all diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes, used BMI as the obesity measure, and excluded selectively screened studies.
Seventy studies involving 671,945 women were included, comprising 59 cohorts and 11 case-control studies from published and unpublished sources.
Most included studies were of high or medium methodological quality when assessing prepregnancy BMI and gestational diabetes risk.
Gestational diabetes risk was positively associated with prepregnancy BMI, and each 1 kg/m2 BMI increase raised GDM prevalence.
Most included studies were of low or medium methodological quality when assessing prepregnancy BMI and gestational diabetes risk.
The study investigated Bmi-1 expression as a prognostic marker for cervical cancer using retrospectively collected population-based data.
RT-PCR measured Bmi-1 mRNA in cervical cancer and noncancerous tissues, while immunohistochemistry detected Bmi-1 protein in cervical cancer samples.
RNA interference downregulated Bmi-1 expression in HeLa cervical cancer cells, and cytotoxicity was measured using colony formation assays.
High Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis.
RNA interference-mediated Bmi-1 inhibition reduced cancer cell growth, enhanced apoptosis, and induced cell cycle arrest in cervical cancer cells.
Low Bmi-1 expression was significantly correlated with poor tumor differentiation, advanced International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics stage, and positive lymph node metastasis.
The study explored Bmal1 effects on oxaliplatin sensitivity and clinical significance in colorectal cancer.
Three colorectal cancer cell lines were used to test Bmal1-mediated proliferation control and oxaliplatin sensitivity.
Bmal1 overexpression inhibited colorectal cancer cell proliferation and increased oxaliplatin sensitivity in vitro and in vivo.
High Bmal1 expression was associated with longer overall and progression-free survival in oxaliplatin-treated colorectal cancer patients.
Bmal1 may be a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target because it regulates G2-M arrest through the ATM pathway.
Low Bmal1 expression was associated with longer overall and progression-free survival in oxaliplatin-treated colorectal cancer patients.
PERISCOPE compared pioglitazone with glimepiride for coronary atherosclerosis progression in type 2 diabetes patients with coronary artery disease.
Patients underwent coronary intravascular ultrasonography, were randomized to glimepiride or pioglitazone, and completed repeat imaging after 18 months.
Least squares mean percent atheroma volume increased with glimepiride and decreased with pioglitazone.
Pioglitazone improved HbA1c, increased high-density lipoprotein levels, decreased triglycerides, and lowered fasting insulin compared with glimepiride.
Hypoglycemia was more common with glimepiride, while edema, fractures, and decreased hemoglobin occurred more frequently with pioglitazone.
Least squares mean percent atheroma volume increased with glimepiride and increased with pioglitazone.
The randomized trial compared early lumbar disc surgery with prolonged conservative care for sciatica caused by lumbar disc herniation over two years.
Participants were 283 patients with six to twelve weeks of sciatica recruited from nine Dutch hospitals.
Main outcomes included Roland disability scores, leg pain visual analogue scores, and global perceived recovery on a Likert self-rating scale.
Early surgery produced faster leg pain improvement, but the short-term benefit was no longer significant by six months.
Patient satisfaction decreased slightly between one and two years in both early surgery and conservative care groups.
Patient satisfaction increased slightly between one and two years in both early surgery and conservative care groups.
The study determined prevalence and clinical associations of impaired awareness of hypoglycemia in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes.
A validated questionnaire assessed hypoglycemia awareness status in 656 patients with type 1 diabetes over a six-month period.
Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia was present in 29% of patients and was associated with earlier diabetes onset and lower A1C levels.
Severe hypoglycemia rates were higher in patients with impaired awareness than in those without impaired awareness.
Screening for impaired awareness was an important component of routine diabetes care for identifying patients at increased severe hypoglycemia risk.
Impaired awareness of hypoglycemia was absent in 29% of patients and was associated with earlier diabetes onset and lower A1C levels.
Preclinical diastolic dysfunction was defined as normal systolic function with diastolic dysfunction and no heart failure symptoms.
Patients had moderate or severe diastolic dysfunction by Doppler criteria, preserved ejection fraction, and no heart failure diagnosis.
Primary endpoints were heart failure by Framingham criteria or symptoms including dyspnoea, oedema, or fatigue.
Hypertension, coronary artery disease, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and reduced creatinine clearance were common among PDD subjects.
Clinical heart failure progression over two years was low, while symptom development and cardiac hospitalisations were moderate in PDD patients.
Clinical heart failure progression over two years was high, while symptom development and cardiac hospitalisations were moderate in PDD patients.
The trial compared oral semaglutide with placebo and subcutaneous semaglutide for glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes.
The 26-week randomized trial enrolled patients with insufficient glycemic control using diet and exercise alone or stable metformin.
Participants received multiple once-daily oral semaglutide doses, oral placebo, or once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide for 26 weeks.
HbA1c levels decreased with oral semaglutide and subcutaneous semaglutide more than with placebo.
Oral semaglutide resulted in better glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Oral semaglutide resulted in worse glycemic control than placebo over 26 weeks in patients with type 2 diabetes.
The POSEIDON trial compared allogeneic and autologous mesenchymal stem cells delivered by transendocardial injection in ischemic cardiomyopathy patients with ventricular dysfunction.
Thirty patients received 20 million, 100 million, or 200 million cells injected into ten left ventricular sites, with thirteen-month follow-up.
The primary outcome assessed thirty-day treatment-emergent serious adverse events after catheterization, while efficacy assessments included functional capacity and ventricular remodeling.
Allogeneic and autologous MSCs reduced early enhancement defect and sphericity index, but did not increase ejection fraction overall.
Transendocardial MSC injection was associated with low rates of treatment-emergent serious adverse events, including immunologic reactions.
Transendocardial MSC injection was associated with high rates of treatment-emergent serious adverse events, including immunologic reactions.
Tafamidis is a transthyretin stabilizer studied in symptomatic ATTR patients, especially beyond early-onset Val30Met disease.
Patients received standardized medical, cardiological, and neurological assessments every six months for up to three years.
Tafamidis proved safe and well-tolerated, although many patients still showed neurological or cardiac disease progression.
Neurological worsening was greatest in the first six months, then slowed significantly during later follow-up.
Higher baseline mBMI was associated with better preservation of neurological function in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
Higher baseline mBMI was associated with worse preservation of neurological function in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis.
The meta-analysis evaluated single baseline Elecsys Troponin T high-sensitive assay measurement for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction in emergency department patients.
Diagnostic accuracy studies were identified through Medline, Embase, and other databases, then assessed with the adapted QUADAS-2 tool.
At the 3-5 ng/L cut-off, summary sensitivity was higher and summary specificity was lower than at 14 ng/L.
Lower cut-off values such as 3 ng/L or 5 ng/L could help rule out acute myocardial infarction.
Care was needed because assay imprecision and lot-to-lot reagent variation had greater effects at low troponin concentrations.
Care was needed because assay imprecision and lot-to-lot reagent variation had greater effects at high troponin concentrations.
The study tested whether elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels could predict hypertension development during long-term follow-up of initially normotensive subjects.
In Uku town, Japan, fasting plasma TGF-β1 data were collected from health examination participants, including 149 normotensives followed for 14 years.
Among 149 normotensives at baseline, 59 subjects developed hypertension, and plasma TGF-β1 levels were significantly associated with hypertension development.
The highest TGF-β1 group had a significant odds ratio for hypertension development compared with the lowest TGF-β1 group after confounder adjustment.
The study concluded that elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels predicted the development of hypertension in community-dwelling Japanese normotensives.
The study concluded that elevated plasma TGF-β1 levels predicted the development of hypotension in community-dwelling Japanese normotensives.
The 1987 ACR classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis were criticized for limited sensitivity in early disease, motivating new RA classification criteria.
A joint ACR and EULAR working group developed a new approach for classifying rheumatoid arthritis in patients with undifferentiated inflammatory synovitis.
The criteria identified patients at high risk for persistent or erosive disease, reflecting the appropriate current paradigm underlying rheumatoid arthritis.
Definite rheumatoid arthritis classification requires confirmed presence of synovitis in at least one joint and absence of a better alternative diagnosis.
The scoring domains include involved joints, serological abnormality, elevated acute-phase response, and symptom duration, with a possible total score of ten.
Definite rheumatoid arthritis classification requires confirmed presence of synovitis in at most one joint and absence of a better alternative diagnosis.
The review integrated neurodevelopmental outcome data after a single course of antenatal corticosteroids for threatened preterm labor.
Included studies reported outcomes for children whose mothers received antenatal betamethasone or dexamethasone, compared with placebo or no treatment.
Antenatal corticosteroids reduced cerebral palsy, low psychomotor development index, and severe disability, while increasing intact survival.
Betamethasone was found to significantly decrease the risk for severe disability and increase the rate of intact survival.
Major limitations included nonrandomized studies and scarce data on finer neurodevelopmental outcomes after antenatal corticosteroid exposure.
Betamethasone was found to significantly increase the risk for severe disability and increase the rate of intact survival.
The study examined whether chronic pulmonary exposure to single-walled carbon nanotubes could promote lung cancer risks through cellular and molecular carcinogenesis processes.
Human lung epithelial cells were chronically exposed to dispersed SWCNT for six months at a physiologically relevant surface area dose.
Chronic SWCNT-exposed cells were evaluated for CSC-like cells under tumor sphere and side population conditions.
CSC-like cells showed apoptosis resistance, increased migration and invasion in vitro, and tumor-initiating capability in vivo.
Detection of CSC and associated surface markers may provide an effective screening tool for predicting carcinogenic potential of SWCNT and related nanoparticles.
Detection of CSC and associated surface markers may provide an ineffective screening tool for predicting carcinogenic potential of SWCNT and related nanoparticles.
The study examined whether funnel plot asymmetry could predict discordance between meta-analyses and later large trials.
Medline searches identified pairs consisting of a meta-analysis and a single large trial with comparable effect directions.
The main outcome was funnel plot asymmetry measured by regression of standard normal deviates against precision.
Eight meta-analysis and large-trial pairs were identified, including four concordant and four discordant pairs.
Funnel plot asymmetry was present in three of four discordant pairs but in none of the concordant pairs.
Funnel plot asymmetry was absent in three of four discordant pairs but in none of the concordant pairs.
Pregnancy in women with renal diseases has important consequences for fetal development and maternal health through anatomical, hemodynamic, and endocrine kidney changes.
Failure to adapt can aggravate maternal renal disease, impair fetal development, and increase the risk of obstetric complications.
Correct interpretation of renal functional tests helps avoid incorrect renal disease diagnosis during pregnancy.
Nephrologists and urologists should manage severe conditions such as preeclampsia, acute and chronic renal failure, dialysis, and renal transplant patients.

The chapter focuses on common preexisting renal diseases in pregnancy, including chronic glomerulonephritis, secondary glomerular nephropathies, interstitial nephropathies, diabetes nephropathy, and chronic renal failure.

The chapter focuses on common preexisting renal diseases in pregnancy, including chronic glomerulonephritis, primary glomerular nephropathies, interstitial nephropathies, diabetes nephropathy, and chronic renal failure.
Hydroxyethyl starches are synthetic colloids used for fluid resuscitation, but their effects on kidney function remain controversial.
The review compared HES with alternate fluid therapies for preventing or treating effective intravascular volume depletion.
Primary outcomes included renal replacement therapy, author-defined kidney failure, and acute kidney injury defined by RIFLE criteria.
HES-treated individuals had higher kidney failure risk and renal replacement therapy requirement than patients receiving other fluid therapies.
Only limited data were available for kidney outcomes by RIFLE criteria, although overall methodological study quality was good.
Only limited data were available for kidney outcomes by RIFLE criteria, although overall methodological study quality was bad.
The study evaluated reagent test strips for screening pregnant women for asymptomatic bacteriuria at their first antenatal clinic visit.
The prospective case series was conducted in a large inner-city maternity hospital antenatal clinic.
A midstream urine specimen was divided; half went for microscopy and culture, and half used a reagent strip for presence of blood, protein, nitrite, and leucocyte esterase.
Outcome measures included sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values for diagnosing asymptomatic bacteriuria.
Urine reagent strips were not sufficiently sensitive, so formal bacteriological investigation remained preferred for pregnant women.
A midstream urine specimen was divided; half went for microscopy and culture, and half used a reagent strip for absence of blood, protein, nitrite, and leucocyte esterase.
FOCUS2 investigated reduced-dose chemotherapy options and objective predictors of outcome in frail patients with advanced colorectal cancer.
Patients with previously untreated advanced colorectal cancer were assigned to fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, capecitabine, or combined chemotherapy groups.
Primary outcomes assessed oxaliplatin addition by progression-free survival and capecitabine substitution by global quality of life change.
Adding oxaliplatin suggested some improvement in progression-free survival, but the finding was not significant in the FOCUS2 factorial comparison.
Fewer baseline symptoms, less widespread disease, and oxaliplatin use predicted better overall treatment utility.
Adding oxaliplatin suggested some decline in progression-free survival, but the finding was not significant in the FOCUS2 factorial comparison.
Elevated plasma total homocysteine was described as a major risk factor for coronary artery disease in the Korean gene-nutrition study.
The MTHFR C677T mutation decreases enzyme activity and contributes to increased homocysteine levels and decreased folate levels.
Researchers screened the MTHFR C677T polymorphism using real-time PCR with melting point analysis in CAD patients and controls.
The genotype-specific folate threshold level was significantly higher in TT individuals than in CC or CT genotype groups.
Individuals with low folate status and the TT genotype had elevated relative risk of coronary artery disease.
Individuals with high folate status and the TT genotype had elevated relative risk of coronary artery disease.
ALTS evaluated immediate colposcopy, cytologic follow-up, and HPV DNA triage for ASCUS or LSIL cervical cytologic interpretations.
Patients with ASCUS or LSIL were randomized to research arms and monitored for histologic CIN 3 or cancer over two years.
Oncogenic HPV prevalence was too high to permit effective LSIL triage using Hybrid Capture 2 HPV DNA testing.
For ASCUS, HPV triage proved useful, with sensitivity equivalent to immediate colposcopy and fewer colposcopic referrals.
Among older women with ASCUS, HPV testing remained sensitive for detecting CIN 3 and cancer, with lower referral percentages than younger women.
Among older women with ASCUS, HPV testing remained insensitive for detecting CIN 3 and cancer, with lower referral percentages than younger women.
Many lung cancer patients have comorbid chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, which may limit stage-specific treatment because of poor lung function.
The study examined pulmonologist management, recommended stage-specific treatment, and survival among NSCLC patients with preexisting COPD.
Early and advanced NSCLC cases with prior COPD were identified from SEER registry data linked to Medicare claims.
Pulmonologist involvement was recorded when evaluation and management claims with pulmonologist specialty appeared within six months after NSCLC diagnosis.
Pulmonologist management had a positive association with stage-specific treatment rates and overall survival in early-stage NSCLC.
Pulmonologist management had a neutral association with stage-specific treatment rates and overall survival in early-stage NSCLC.
The FRONTLINE study surveyed oncologists about perceived venous thromboembolism risk and practice patterns in cancer patients undergoing surgical and medical management.
A paper-based questionnaire was distributed globally to clinicians involved in cancer care and made available on a dedicated website.
Brain and pancreatic tumors were considered to carry a high risk for VTE in the FRONTLINE survey of cancer thrombosis practice.
Low molecular weight heparin was the most popular thromboprophylaxis method in both surgical and medical cancer patients.
The survey showed a need for evidence-based guidelines concerning cancer-associated VTE prevention and treatment.
Brain and pancreatic tumors were considered to carry a low risk for VTE in the FRONTLINE survey of cancer thrombosis practice.
The NCS-R presented nationally representative data on major depressive disorder prevalence, correlates, treatment patterns, and treatment adequacy using DSM-IV criteria.
The face-to-face household survey included 9,090 United States residents aged 18 years or older who responded to the NCS-R.
Outcome measures included CIDI prevalence, QIDS-SR severity, the Sheehan Disability Scale, and the WHO disability assessment scale.
Virtually all 12-month CIDI cases were clinically significant, with severity classified as mild, moderate, severe, or very severe.
Major depressive disorder was described as a common disorder with substantial symptom severity and role impairment in the National Comorbidity Survey Replication conclusions.
Major depressive disorder was described as an uncommon disorder with substantial symptom severity and role impairment in the National Comorbidity Survey Replication conclusions.
Nanotoxicology evaluates potential hazards of engineered nanostructures and nanodevices using evidence from biokinetic, epidemiologic, and toxicologic studies of ultrafine particles.
Inhaled nanosized particles are deposited by diffusional mechanisms across respiratory regions and can reach target sites such as bone marrow, spleen, and heart.
Small particle size facilitates uptake into cells and transcytosis across epithelial and endothelial cells into blood and lymph circulation.
Nanosized particle biokinetics are largely dependent on surface chemistry and in vivo surface modifications.
Nanotoxicology risk assessment should include careful selection of appropriate doses and concentrations for engineered nanosized particles.
Large particle size facilitates uptake into cells and transcytosis across epithelial and endothelial cells into blood and lymph circulation.
Cytotoxic T cell activation by antigen requires specific detection of pMHC molecules on the target-cell surface by the T cell receptor.
The study examined mutations in Kb-restricted TCR antigen-binding sites and variants from a Kd-restricted peptide recognized by cytotoxic T cell clones.
Mutations that decreased or increased the binding half-life of the TCR-pMHC interaction impaired T cell activation in two independent systems.
Efficient T cell activation occurred within an optimal dwell-time range of TCR-pMHC interaction, rather than simply requiring stronger antigen binding.
The restricted dwell-time range was consistent with excluding extremely low or high affinity T cells from expanded populations during immune responses.
The restricted dwell-time range was inconsistent with excluding extremely low or high affinity T cells from expanded populations during immune responses.
The study examined IL-10 regulation of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis using transgenic mice expressing human IL-10 under a class II MHC promoter.
Human IL-10 transgenic mice were highly resistant to EAE induced by active immunization through suppression of autoreactive T cell function.
Myelin-reactive T helper 1 cells were induced but remained nonpathogenic in IL-10 transgenic mice.
Transgenic IL-10 from MHC class II-expressing cells was sufficient to block induction of EAE.
IL-10 prevented EAE completely when present at appropriate levels and times during disease induction in the transgenic mouse model.
IL-10 prevented EAE completely when present at inappropriate levels and times during disease induction in the transgenic mouse model.
The study examined biochemical and conformational differences in alphabeta TCR.CD3 surface complexes between CD4-positive and CD8-positive human mature T lymphocytes.
Surface TCR.CD3 components from CD4-positive CD3gamma-deficient T cells were detectable and similar in size to normal CD4-positive controls.
In CD8-positive CD3gamma-deficient T cells, TCRalpha was hardly detectable and blue native gels showed heterogeneous TCR.CD3 populations.
RW2-8C8 stained CD8-positive T cells better than CD4-positive T cells, with differences dependent on TCR.CD3 glycosylation.
Immunoprecipitation studies revealed the existence of TCR glycosylation differences between purified primary CD4-positive and CD8-positive T cells.
Immunoprecipitation studies revealed the nonexistence of TCR glycosylation differences between purified primary CD4-positive and CD8-positive T cells.
Diabetes is a group of chronic diseases characterized by hyperglycemia, while treatment aims to reduce vascular harm from elevated glucose.
Hyperglycemia damages the human vascular tree and is a major source of morbidity and mortality in type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
Macrovascular complications include coronary artery disease, peripheral arterial disease, and stroke, while microvascular complications include nephropathy, neuropathy, and retinopathy.
Diabetic retinopathy is a common microvascular complication and causes thousands of new blindness cases each year in the United States.
Retinopathy risk depends on both duration and severity of hyperglycemia, and may begin before type 2 diabetes diagnosis.

The review examined evidence for specific suicide-preventive interventions and recommendations for future prevention programs and research.
Studies covered public and professional education, at-risk screening tools, psychiatric treatment, restricting lethal means, and responsible media reporting.
Data extraction focused on suicidal behavior, treatment seeking, identification of at-risk individuals, antidepressant prescription rates, and referrals.
Education of physicians and restricting access to lethal means were found to prevent suicide.
Identifying effective components of suicide prevention programs was essential for reducing suicide and suicide attempt rates.
Identifying ineffective components of suicide prevention programs was essential for reducing suicide and suicide attempt rates.
Recent studies suggest that betaKlotho and endocrine FGF19 and FGF21 redirect FGFR signaling toward metabolic homeostasis and suppression of obesity and diabetes.
The study determined receptor and tissue specificity of FGF21 compared with FGF19 using binding kinetics and downstream signal transduction.
FGF21 bound FGFR1 with higher affinity than FGFR4 in the presence of KLB, whereas FGF19 bound both receptors comparably.
The FGF21 interaction with FGFR4-KLB was very weak at high concentration and negligible at physiological concentration.
FGF21 was unable to bind the FGFR4-KLB complex with affinity comparable to FGFR1-KLB at physiological concentration.
FGF21 was able to bind the FGFR4-KLB complex with affinity comparable to FGFR1-KLB at physiological concentration.
Pyruvate dehydrogenase regulates skeletal muscle substrate utilization, and the study examined whether muscle IL-6 contributes to exercise-induced PDH regulation during treadmill exercise.
Skeletal muscle-specific IL-6 knockout mice and floxed controls completed 10, 60, or 120 minutes of treadmill exercise, with rested mice as basal controls.
The respiratory exchange ratio was higher in IL-6 MKO mice than controls, while RER decreased during exercise independent of genotype.
PDHa activity was higher in control mice during exercise than at rest, but remained unchanged in IL-6 MKO mice.
